title: Hidden Gems in Ston, Croatia: Local Spots 2027
metaDescription: Quiet coves, fishing hamlets and local food stops around Ston, Croatia that most day-trippers skip, with distances, prices and practical tips for 2027.
content:
## Which Ston Spots Do Most Visitors Miss?

Most day-trippers from Dubrovnik arrive by 10:00, walk the walls, eat oysters in Mali Ston and leave by mid-afternoon. The municipality covers about 169 km² but has only around 2,500 residents (2021 census). That leaves a lot of quiet coast. This guide covers the villages, coves and food stops that sit outside the standard route.

## Broce: A Pine-Shaded Cove 2 km from Ston

Broce is a village of about 90 people, two kilometers from Ston, surrounded by thick pine forest, with a beach reachable by boat. It has a Dominican convent dating from 1628. Bring your own water and snacks, because services are minimal. It is a good option for a swim when Prapratno fills up in July and August.

## Kobaš: The Cove at the End of the Road

The road to Kobaš is winding and only a few kilometres long, and it ends at one of the most stunning coves in the southern Adriatic. Drive slowly and avoid midday in peak season, since parking is tight. Go before 10:00 or after 17:00.

## The Mali Ston Bay Hamlets

Zamaslina, Hodilje, Luka, Malo Selo and Duba Stonska are small villages a few kilometres north of Ston. Zamaslina has only about 70 residents. The hamlets are former fishing settlements, and their coastal road follows the bay where oysters and mussels are farmed. Stop where you see a family-run konoba or a farm sign, and ask what was harvested that day.

Oyster prices at local restaurants run about €1.50-3 each. Boat trips into the farms with oysters pulled from the water usually cost €15-22 per person. One festival-time boat tour sold at Bota Šare restaurant in Mali Ston cost €22 and included five oysters and a glass of wine.

Skip the €170-260 full-service tours from Dubrovnik if you have a car. The same oysters, boat ride and wine cost a fraction of that when booked directly at the bay.

## Podzvizd at Sunset

The hill above Ston is a short climb from the old town. Ston lies at the foot of Podzvizd hill, and the late-afternoon light over the salt pans and bay is best between 18:00 and 20:00 in summer. Wear real shoes because the stone is loose. This is a better use of your evening than a crowded bar terrace.

## Prapratno Before 10:00

Prapratno is not a secret, but it is nearly empty early. It is one of the rare sandy beaches in Croatia. The Mljet ferry leaves from here, and day-trippers rush through. Arrive before the ferry crowds and you can swim in calm, shallow water with the pines behind you.

## Local Food Worth Seeking Out

- **Ston rafioli:** a traditional almond-and-spice pastry sold in bakeries in the old town. Buy it fresh in the morning.
- **Mussels buzara-style:** often cheaper than oysters and just as local.
- **Pelješac wines:** Plavac Mali reds and Pošip or Rukatac whites. Winery tastings generally cost about €20 per person for three glasses.

## Practical Tips

- **Getting there:** Ston is about 55 km from Dubrovnik via the Pelješac Bridge, roughly 55-65 minutes by car. The public bus costs about €8 one way and takes around 1.5 hours, but it does not serve the villages.
- **Best time:** May, June and late September. In July and August, start before 09:00.
- **Transport:** A car is the easiest option. A bicycle also works for the Ston-Broce-Mali Ston stretch, since distances are short.
- **Where to stay:** Mali Ston has small waterfront guesthouses. Prapratno suits beach-focused stays.
- **Cash:** Small farms and family konobas often prefer cash, so carry some.

## Frequently Asked Questions

See the FAQ section below for quick answers.

faq.question: What are the best hidden gems in Ston, Croatia?
faq.answer: The best lesser-known spots are the Broce cove, the Kobaš bay, the fishing hamlets of Zamaslina, Hodilje and Duba Stonska, and the Podzvizd hill at sunset. All are free to visit and lie within a few kilometres of Ston town.

faq.question: Do I need a car to explore Ston's off-the-beaten-path spots?
faq.answer: A car is the easiest option, as the public bus from Dubrovnik (about €8 one way) only reaches Ston town. Broce is only 2 km away, so cycling also works for the closest villages.

faq.question: How much do oysters cost in Ston?
faq.answer: Oysters in local restaurants cost about €1.50-3 each. Boat trips into the farms with tasting typically run €15-22 per person when booked locally, much less than tours from Dubrovnik.

faq.question: When is the quietest time to visit Ston?
faq.answer: May, June and late September are the quietest months. In summer, arriving before 09:00 or after 17:00 avoids most day-trip crowds from Dubrovnik.

quickAnswer: The best hidden gems in Ston are outside the walls: the pine-shaded cove at Broce (2 km), the Kobaš bay, the fishing hamlets of Zamaslina, Hodilje and Duba Stonska on Mali Ston Bay, and the Podzvizd hilltop at sunset. All are free, and a car or bike makes them easy.
